title: Georgia Elects Keisha Lance Bottoms as First Black Woman Governor in U.S. History
summary: Georgia voters made history this week. They elected Keisha Lance Bottoms as the state's first Democratic governor in more than two decades, and the first Black woman ever elected governor in the United States. Bottoms is the former mayor of Atlanta. She campaigned on lowering the cost of living, expanding health care, and pushing back against the Trump administration. She will take office in a state where Republicans still control the Senate, so she will need their support to pass many of her plans. Her family has lived in Georgia for at least five generations. She can trace her roots to a plantation in Crawfordville, where her great-great-grandparents were once enslaved. She said being elected governor has exceeded every dream she ever had for her life. Bottoms said the win came from decades of work by people across Georgia. Georgia has not elected a Democratic governor since 1998. Her message is to listen to voters and focus on daily life, especially the cost of living. Democrats also won the Georgia House and are one seat away from controlling the Senate.
why_it_matters: A governor helps make choices about things that touch your family's daily life, like the cost of living and health care.

Enslaved means forced to work for someone else with no freedom and no pay.
Generations are the people in a family who live at different times, like grandparents, parents, and children.
